did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens by introducing Elkanah and his family lineage: he was the son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, and he is described as an Ephrathite.
Did you know? Every year, Elkanah went up to Shiloh to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts. At that time, Eli’s sons, Hophni and Phinehas, served there as priests of the LORD.
Did you know? Elkanah distributed portions of the sacrifice to all the members of his family, illustrating the family meal that accompanied worship at Shiloh.
Did you know? Elkanah gave Hannah a special portion out of his love for her, even though she was barren. The chapter explicitly states that the LORD had closed her womb.
Did you know? The journey to Shiloh took place every year, but instead of being only a time of joy for Hannah, it was marked by Peninnah’s provocation, weeping, and refusal to eat.

Did you know? In her vow, Hannah asked for a son and promised to dedicate him to the LORD all the days of his life. Among the signs of his dedication, she mentioned: “No razor shall ever be used on his head.”
Did you know? Hannah prayed without making a sound: her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. Eli saw her behavior and mistakenly thought she was drunk.
Did you know? After Hannah explained to Eli that she was pouring out her soul before the LORD, he blessed her and prayed that the LORD would grant her request.
Did you know? After Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son, she named him Samuel, because, as she said, she had asked the LORD for him. Thus, the text connects Samuel’s name with her prayer.
Did you know? After Samuel was weaned, Hannah brought him to Shiloh with bulls, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine, in order to fulfill her dedication of him to the LORD.
